newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cellphone operators face uphill battle in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Cellphone operators face uphill battle in Pakistan.

text.p: Mobile telephone operators are at odds with Pakistani authorities despite months of talks with successive governments, industry sources said on Tuesday.

The three cellular telephone firms operating in Pakistan are dismayed by reports that Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL), the state-run telephone utility, might apply for a licence for its own cellular network, the sources said.
The official news agency APP this week quoted official sources as saying that Communications Minister Azam Hoti had told PTCL to operate its own mobile telephone network.
However, an official at the ministry denied the report. "He (Hoti) never said that," the official said. "He said that there was no intention of introducing a fourth cellular operator."
A PTCL official said the utility had made no request for a licence to operate a cellular telephone network.
APP also said Hoti had "expressed his displeasure over the commercial ethics of the existing cellular operators, who are looting the people at the expense of the PTCL".

The operators -- Pakcom Ltd, a subsidiary of Luxembourg's Millicom International Paktel Ltd, a Cable & Wireless subsidiary; and Pakistan Mobile Telecommunications, a joint venture of U.S.-based Motorola Inc and local Saif Telecom -- say any new licence would contravene the terms of their own licences.

They complain that they have suffered a negative average return on capital employed of 36 percent and accumulated losses of 2.2 billion rupees ($53.9 million) due to erratic decisions by the government, high taxes and low air-time tariffs.

They also say they are still awaiting a relief package promised by the previous caretaker government for a 19-month ban on mobile telephone services in Karachi, imposed for security reasons by the former government led by Benazir Bhutto.

"They are now being told that they have to cover the whole of Pakistan with their networks, despite this being in contradiction to their licences, which say they have to cover only four cities and other cities wherever economically and commercially practical," one industry source said.
He said the PTCL was pressing the operators to stop offering their customers discounts, saying this deprived PTCL of revenue.

The official at the Communications Ministry, who asked not to be named, said the ministry had always been "sympathetic" to the industry's concerns, adding that the operators had voluntarily foregone compensation for the Karachi shutdown.
After hearing a joint presentation of the operators' case on Friday, Hoti had formed a committee to look into their grievances and report back within 15 days, one industry source said.
Demands set out by the operators in a document obtained by Reuters include reducing import duties and cutting customs and excise duty and advance income tax to pre-June 1996 levels.

They also asked for an interconnect agreement with PTCL to conform with internationally accepted standards, a free market for tariffs and suppliers, adherence to licence conditions and a government strategy for the telecommunication sector to facilitate long-term investment decisions by the operators.
